# I had an AI build a safety KY and morning briefing board: confirmation and signature components made for health care and accounting worked unchanged for construction safety (build log #176)

> **Build log series**: I hand my own design system `@gunjo/ui` ([Gunjo](https://gunjo.jp)) to an AI that has never seen it, and have it build real screens. This is the third construction screen. The brief: a **safety KY (hazard prediction) board for the morning briefing on a construction site**. It brings together the hazards and precautions for each task that day, attendance and acknowledgment from participants, finalization of the record, and approval from the person in charge.

## Result: 4/5. The confirmation and signature components carried across industries into safety management

I gave an AI that had never seen Gunjo nothing but the public npm package and the gunjo.jp docs, and asked it to build the screen. `tsc` passed clean, and the screen works on both mobile and desktop.

The highlight this time is that **components added to Gunjo for confirmation and signatures in health care and accounting worked unchanged for safety management on a construction site**.

- **`SafetyBanner` (highest-priority instruction)**: this acknowledgment banner blocks progress until it is confirmed. It was originally designed for health care warnings about allergies and contraindications, but it matched the morning briefing instruction "The entire crane swing radius is off-limits. The record cannot be finalized until this is confirmed" unchanged.
- **`SignedRecord` (finalized, then append-only)**: once the foreperson finalizes the record, it is locked and only additions can be made afterward. It matched the safety record requirement that finalized records become append-only.
- **`CoSign` (two-person confirmation)**: this was built for double-checking medication administration and accounting approvals, but it implemented the flow in which "a general contractor supervisor approves the record as a second person, separate from the foreperson" unchanged. It also includes a guard that prevents the same person from approving twice.
- **`DataTable` (roster)**: it worked unchanged as the attendance roster, including its ability to switch from a table on desktop to cards on mobile.

A screen that looks specialized because it deals with safety came together around components from health care and accounting.

## What was missing: KY sheet rows, roster checks, and handwritten signatures

Three areas remained uncovered, and each has a shape specific to construction safety management.

1. **There is no KY sheet row for laying out hazards and precautions.** I wanted one unit that brings together multiple predicted hazards, multiple precautions, risk level, and implementation checks for each task, but there is no such component. The existing checklist components use a structure of one check per row, which does not fit multiple hazards and precautions, so I hand-rolled it (about 75 lines). The rows for confirming implementation could use an existing component unchanged.
2. **There is no roster with checks for multiple attributes.** The table itself already existed for a roster that checks each worker's health, alcohol result, protective equipment, and identity, but I hand-rolled the arrangement of checks and the mobile cards (about 130 lines).
3. **There is no component for collecting a handwritten signature.** There is no component that lets a person sign by actually drawing a line. This time I substituted a checkbox. This is a clear gap because safety and administrative records sometimes require one in real operations.

The hand-rolled portion came to just over 200 lines out of roughly 870 for the whole screen, so it was only one part. However, KY sheets and rosters are common shapes in construction safety management, so they are likely to be needed again on other site screens. I follow the rule of three: a missing component gets built for real only after three separate screens have needed it independently. These three are still at one.

## Where the names got confusing and where they worked well

- **The name `StatusBoard` is confusing.** Because it says "board," I thought it might be the main morning briefing board, but it is actually a tile board for dispatching and monitoring, which is a different thing from a KY sheet.
- This time, on the other hand, **the by-use-case table worked well.** Phrases describing the purpose, such as "two-person confirmation" and "append-only after finalization," led directly to `SafetyBanner`, `CoSign`, and `SignedRecord` through the by-use-case table, a static table that maps what you want to build to the components for it. In the photo management round, the table had no media section and the agent took a detour, but the safety and signature area was organized well. This also revealed that the table's coverage varies by area.

## Wrapping up

The skeleton of the third construction screen also came together from components built for other industries. Confirmation and signature components from health care and accounting worked unchanged for site safety management. The uncovered areas were three shapes specific to safety management: KY sheet rows, a roster with multiple checks, and handwritten signatures. Once again, the components that work in common cover a broad area, while the missing pieces cluster around industry-specific needs.
